subject: Re: Kickoff: HMC posterior reference - status + domain-shift caveat
body:
Status: M1 done, M2 on track. The JAX pipeline reproduces the paper's CIFAR-10 results; consistent with the paper we see no meaningful cold-posterior effect once data augmentation is off, so our reference chains run untempered - one less knob in the product.

Two findings that shape the scoring API:

1) Reassuring: BMA performance is robust to prior scale, and diagonal Gaussian vs. mixture priors barely move results. Rafael signed off on shipping diagonal Gaussian as the sole v1 prior.

2) The caveat: BNN posteriors generalize surprisingly poorly under domain shift - on CIFAR-10-C our HMC reference gets outperformed by plain deep ensembles on 12 of 16 corruptions. So the calibration report must carry an explicit in-distribution disclaimer, or we'll be scoring customers against a reference that's wrong exactly when they care most.

Proposal: v1 scopes to in-distribution only; domain-shift extension becomes a Q3 item.

Efe
